content.intro: This lesson covers Secure Communication and TLS Integration. It sits in Module 21, Serialization, Networking, and APIs, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Secure Communication and TLS Integration matters when you work with validated data crossing a network boundary. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Networked systems exchange data across an unreliable boundary. Define framing and schemas, validate input, use timeouts, handle partial failures, and avoid retrying non-idempotent operations blindly.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Secure Communication and TLS Integration, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Standard-library examples cover protocol fundamentals; production serialization, HTTP clients, TLS and async networking usually require selecting maintained ecosystem crates.
